paper.title: From Bandits to Experts: On the Value of Side-Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Side-observations with fixed graph G_t = G (ExpBan)
unmapped: side observations are unbiased estimates of neighbours' rewards bounded in absolute value by b (not exact rewards)
graph may be directed; learner needs a clique partition of G
settings.definition_quote: we assume that one receives $g_i(t)$, and for some fixed parameter $b$ is able to construct unbiased estimates $\hat{g}_j(t)$ for all actions $j$ in some subset of $[k]$, such that $\E[\hat{g}_j(t)|\text{action i  chosen}]=g_j(t)$ and $\Pr(|\hat{g}_j(t)|\leq b)=1$. ... We assume that $N_j(t)$ for all $j,t$ are known to the learner in advance.

settings.name_in_paper: Side-observations with time-varying undirected graphs G_t (ELP)
unmapped: side observations are unbiased estimates bounded by b
settings.definition_quote: In the case that $j\in N_i(t)$ if and only if $i\in N_j(t)$, for all $i,j$, we say that $G_t$ is undirected. ... We assume that $N_j(t)$ for all $j,t$ are known to the learner in advance.

settings.name_in_paper: Side-observations with time-varying directed graphs G_t (ELP)
unmapped: side observations are unbiased estimates bounded by b
settings.definition_quote: a natural extension of this setting is to assume a directed graph, where choosing an action $i$ may give us information on the reward of action $j$, but not vice-versa.

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed graph G with no side-observations between non-linked actions (lower bound)
unmapped: actions not linked in G get no side-observations whatsoever between them
settings.definition_quote: Suppose $G_t = G$ for all $t$, and that actions which are not linked in $G$ get no side-observations whatsoever between them.

algorithms.name: ExpBan (exponentially weighted forecaster per clique + EXP3 over cliques)
ELP (Exponentially-weighted algorithm with Linear Programming)

symbols.c_part: number of cliques in the clique partition used; equals clique-partition number chi_bar(G) for the optimal partition

conditions: G_t = G fixed for all rounds

source.label: thm:simple
source.quote: Suppose $G_t=G$ is fixed for all $T$ rounds. If we run ExpBan using the exponentially weighted forecaster and the EXP3 algorithm, then the expected regret is bounded as follows: \sum_{t=1}^{T}g_j(t)-\E[\sum_{t=1}^{T}g_{i_t}(t)] \leq 4b\sqrt{c\log(k)T}. For the optimal clique partition, we have $c=\bar{\chi}(G)$, the clique-partition number of $G$.

results.notes: Oblivious adversary, so expected regret vs fixed j equals pseudo-regret form. Computing the optimal clique partition is NP-hard; with c = chi_bar(G) the bound is 4b sqrt(chi_bar(G) log(k) T).

symbols.sum_alpha: sum over t of the independence number alpha(G_t)

tuning: gamma(t) = beta b / min_j sum_{l in N_j(t)} s_l(t)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Suppose that for all $t$, $G_t$ is an undirected graph. Suppose we run \algref{alg:bandits} using some $\beta\in(0,1/2bk)$, and choosing ... Then it holds for any fixed action $j$ that ... \leq 3\beta b^2\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha(G_t)+\frac{\log(k)}{\beta}.

results.notes: Paper's learning rate beta renamed eta. LP solved per round, so polynomial.

symbols.sum_alpha: sum over t of the independence number alpha(G_t)

tuning: gamma(t) = beta b / min_j sum_{l in N_j(t)} s_l(t)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If we choose $\beta= \sqrt{\log(k)/3b^2\sum_t\alpha(G_t)}$, then the bound equals b\sqrt{3\log(k)\sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha(G_t)}.

results.notes: Tuning requires knowledge of sum_t alpha(G_t) (NP-hard to compute); paper discusses a log(k)-copies EXP3 workaround with extra O(sqrt(log^2(k) T)) regret, not a formal theorem. Tuning must also respect beta < 1/(2bk).

conditions: actions not linked in G get no side-observations between them
randomized adversary (Bernoulli rewards, one arm with mean 1/2+eps)

source.label: th:lowerbound
source.quote: Suppose $G_t = G$ for all $t$, and that actions which are not linked in $G$ get no side-observations whatsoever between them. Then there exists a (randomized) adversary strategy, such that for every $T\ge 374 \alpha(G)^3 $ and any learning strategy, the expected regret is at least $0.06 \sqrt{\alpha(G) T}$.

results.notes: Proof via reduction to Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi Thm 6.11 with stochastic Bernoulli adversary; regret measured in expectation over randomized adversary. Footnote: with max degree d, holds for T >= Omega(d^2 alpha(G)). Quantity type (pseudo vs expected regret) somewhat ambiguous.
